concerns: The cue is broad: Indonesian "pesisir" more specifically denotes a coastal area, while Malaysian "pantai" commonly covers coast or beach.
Indonesian "pantai" is also ordinary for geographic coast, weakening the claimed national preference.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers can fit the broad geographic sense of land along the sea, though "pantai" may also specifically mean beach.
material_concerns: The pair may mislead learners into treating "pesisir" as the Indonesian equivalent and "pantai" as the Malaysian equivalent, although "pantai" is common in Indonesian coast names and descriptions.

preference_risk.rationale: "Pantai" is plausibly ordinary for the coast sense in both Indonesian and Malaysian, limiting the usefulness of the proposed contrast.

response.rationale: Both forms can refer to land along the sea, but the contrast is not a clean national split. "Pantai" is ordinary in both varieties, while "pesisir" is more specialized or formal in Malaysian usage.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: The shared form "pantai" is ordinary for coast in Indonesian as well as Malaysian, especially in geographic names and regional descriptions, so it can defeat the proposed preference.
